senses.sense: The spiritual and vital power in things from which their natural actions, and the actions of cures, proceed, as against the bodies and their qualities.

evidence.quote: all Naturall actions proceed from Spirits and spirituall Tinctures
the actions of Cures proceed from the Spirits and vitall Tinctures of the spirits, not from the bodies or dead Relloceous qualities

senses.sense: Something some bodies have in which the qualities agree though no actions proceed from them; and a 'Radicall Tincture' that, with the Balsam, preserves the Elements in all things.

evidence.quote: some bodies doe imitate the properties or qualities of Seeds, and have the Tinctures in which though heat, cold, moysture and drinesse accord, yet no actions proceed from them
mingled with and preserved by the Balsam and Radicall Tincture

senses.sense: New Tinctures that came in by God's curse after the fall; the bracket calls them infinite evils.

evidence.quote: by the curse of God new Tinctures came in (even infinite evills)

senses.sense: A quality named beside colour and form, which precious stones take from a metal by the stars; each kind of stone has the Tincture of one metal.

evidence.quote: precious stones have the Colour, Forme and Tincture more or lesse from Mettalls by formation of the Stars
Rubies and Garnats have the Tincture of Gold

senses.sense: The chief medicine: a margin note says the Tincture is the Fift Essence of the Microcosm (margin note only).

evidence.quote: The Tincture is the Fife Essence of the Microcosm

senses.sense: The true thing sought in the work, set against the mere colour that the foolish find instead.

evidence.quote: instead of the Tincture they should find only the colour

senses.sense: Something that cleanses the Balsom, with an effect seen to the tenth generation (margin note only).

evidence.quote: The Tincture doth so cleanse the Balsom, that our children in the tenth generation may see the effect of it

senses.sense: Said of the Astra's of the Firmament in relation to the mind: they are called the Tincture of its speculation; the lines given do not say more (rests on one word of the translation).

evidence.quote: all the Astra's of the Firmament, which are the Tincture of the speculation of our mind

senses.sense: Part of the name of a writing of Paracelsus cited by the author.

evidence.quote: which Paracelsus in the Tincture of Physicks explaineth
Paracelsus in the Tincture of medicines.

senses.sense: The three things every body is made of and resolved into, shown when it is opened by art: the lines point to Mercury, Sulphur and Salt.

evidence.quote: the Three First discover themselves with their hidden vertues
the Physicall body is nothing else but Sulphur, Salt and Mercury
in their Three First (principles) with their garments put off; made naked and visible
a most limpid or clear MERCURIAL, a most garnished SULPHUREAN or oyly, and a most bright pure SALINE form

senses.sense: The three from which all compound bodies come and into which they are resolved, found in every matrix.

evidence.quote: from the three first are all compound bodies, into which they are againe resolved
these three are found in every matrix

senses.sense: The three whose union in a body is health and whose disunion is sickness: the cause of all diseases.

evidence.quote: So that the Three First are the cause of all diseases
in what body soever they are united that may be concluded to be a sound body
The Originall of all diseases is from the Three First upon which the Astra's
Mans health consisteth in the agreement and union of the Three First Substances
the Three First Substances of diseases are valitile

senses.sense: The three whose proportion broken is the origin of bodily diseases, set beside what common physicians call the disorder of the four Elements or Humors.

evidence.quote: the true originall of all corporall diseases, in the judgement of the best Physitians, is the enormity of the Naturall proportion of the Three First

senses.sense: The three first of one particular substance, vinegar, which Galen could not separate; a bracket glosses them as qualities.

evidence.quote: to separate the three first (qualities) in vineger

senses.sense: The three first things of milk: whey, butter and cheese, all earthiness being Salt (margin note only).

evidence.quote: Whey, Butter and Cheese are the three first things of milk, for all Terresterity is Salt

senses.sense: A set of three of which man partakes, named where the metals' use in physic is defended. Reading 1: the same three as elsewhere, of which every body is made. Basis: the phrase as used in CH1.37 and CH1.40. Reading 2: the animal, vegetable and mineral seed named in the next words. Basis: their place directly after.

evidence.quote: although man partaketh of those Three first, let them know that the Animall, Vegetable and Minerall sperm or seed have but one rise or originall

senses.sense: The parting of purity from impurity, or truth from falsehood, given as the meaning of a Spagiricall resolution.

evidence.quote: A seperation of purity from impurity, or truth from falshood
as in a Spagiricall resolution is plainly to be seen

senses.sense: The parting of strong from weak and pure from impure that can be made in certain bodies.

evidence.quote: in such bodies there may be a seperation made of the strong from the weak, of the pure from the impure

senses.sense: The act by which the spiritual Elements set the visible bodies apart from themselves at the making of all things, as the soul parts its body from itself and yet dwells in it.

evidence.quote: so also these spirituall Elements in the seperation of all things have severed the visible bodies from themselves by seperation

senses.sense: A work of each bodily member, named beside its digestion, emunctory and excrement (margin note only).

evidence.quote: Every member hath its own proper digestion, seperation, emunctory, excrement in it selfe

senses.sense: A womb: the place in which a seed or Astrum is received, dies and rots, and brings forth its fruit; the fruits of one Element may be brought forth in the matrix of another.

evidence.quote: the four Astra's of the said Elements are the Seeds in the four matrices or wombs
so soon as ever the Seed or Astrum dies and rots in its matrix or womb, the Astrum goes forward into a new body
For the Astrum of every Element brings forth and bayes its fruits in a strange region or matrix
generating matrix, as the fish in the water

senses.sense: The mother out of which a whole is brought forth: Water is the Matrix of the world, the great world the matrix of Adam (margin notes only).

evidence.quote: Water is the Matrix of the world, upon which the Spirit of God moved
The great world was the matrix of Adam, thus the whole frame of the world is the mother of all things that are brought forth

senses.sense: A place of birth in which the three first are found, as in every birth from it.

evidence.quote: these three are found in every matrix

senses.sense: The invisible part of a star, the Astrum in it, which is the star properly; every thing, sensible or not, has one.

evidence.quote: the invisible Astrum or Sydereall Spirit in the Stars we cannot see; so that not the body of the Sun, but the Spirit in the body, is the Sun properly
That which is sensible and that which is insensible hath a sydereall spirit or a sydereall body in it

senses.sense: In man: the invisible man from the Firmament, the life that dwells in the body and is properly the man; mortal, distinct from the immortal soul breathed in by God; fed from the Firmament, it draws all arts and human wisdom from the stars, leads the body where it imagines, and stirs each man's dexterity.

evidence.quote: which life is the Syderiall Spirit, and is properly the Man, not flesh and blood
As the Syderiall Spirit is the life of the Body, so the Spirit of the Lord is the life of the Intellectuall Soule
the Syderiall spirit of Man or the invisible Man (which is the In-mate of the body) hath its food from the externall Aire and Fire or Firmament
one a syderiall Spirit from the Firmament, the other from the breath of life, which is the Intellectuall Soul inspired from God
Man hath three parts, a mortall Body with a Syderiall Spirit, and an immortall Soule
that Astrall body or Syderiall Spirit, which is the true Astrall Man
This Spirit is mortall
And as the Sydereall Spirit dwells in the Body and works therein day and night
the syderiall spirit of Man attracteth all Arts, sciences, and faculties, and all humane Wisdome from the Rayes or beams of the superiour Stars or constellations
Such is the force of the Sydereall spirit upon the body, that whithersoever it imagineth and dreameth it carryeth and leadeth the very body up and down with it
every man according to his dexterity which the sydereall spirit causeth and exciteth is the forger of his own fortune

senses.sense: A ruler of the Old man in proud men, set against the life of Christ and the holy Spirit named just before.

evidence.quote: who suffer the Old man to be ruled by the Sydereall Spirit

senses.sense: That from which all natural things may be learned, after the stars are said to pierce into man. Reading 1: man's own sydereall spirit, which comes from the Firmament. Basis: MICRO.14 and CH1.41 give man a syderiall spirit from the Firmament that draws wisdom from the stars. Reading 2: the Firmament's own spirit. Basis: the words 'of the Firmament'.

evidence.quote: so that of the syderiall spirit of the Firmament we may learn all Naturall things

senses.sense: In the Chymist's work: the second life a herb or medicine reaches after its first life dies, through putrefaction, in which the three first show their hidden virtues; without it no hid secret of physic is reached.

evidence.quote: 'Tis necessary that the first life of hearbs and medicines should die that the second life by the Chymists help may be attained through Putrefaction and Regeneration
for without Regeneration no hid Secret of Physick can be attained to

senses.sense: The state of the chief medicine, called a whole new regenerate world, by virtue of which it renews man, the little old world.

evidence.quote: this whole new regenerate world is able by vertue of its Regeneration to renew the little old corruptible world Man
the Fift Essence of the whole frame of the world, and the whole world Regenerated

senses.sense: The new birth from God that Christians have and the Heathen lack; it overcomes a bad birth, is glossed as a celestial transplantation, and gives true philosophy and all sciences; Hermes and others knew it before the Word was incarnate and concealed it.

evidence.quote: Christians onely in whom the Truth is planted, who have their seed from God, by the means of Regeneration which the Heathen have not
No Art can be perfected without Regeneration
This Regeneration that holy man Hermes and others of clean hearts and godly lives before the Word was incarnate being enlightned by the holy Spirit
Regeneration overcometh a bad birth
All Sciences are perfectly attained unto by the Fundamentall of Faith and new Regeneration or Celestiall Transplantation
A man cannot have better Phylosophy then f{G162: 1 letter illegible}om God in the Regeneration
a desire of future Blessednesse through the Regeneration

senses.sense: The renewal at the end of this world, according to soul, spirit and body, called in a bracket the New Jerusalem; its time is said to draw nigh.

evidence.quote: at the end of this world which is to be Renewed by the Ternary of Man
the Regeneration according to Soul, Spirit, and Body (the New Jerusalem, wherein the Unitrine Essence of God and the Holy and most Holy Trinity inseperably dwell) will sparkle and glitter out
the time of Revocation and Regeneration drawing nigh, every imperfect thing will of necessity come to nought

senses.sense: Man's second, invisible body, from the Astra's of the Firmament and living by it, the house of the spirit's life and capable of philosophy, as against the visible body from the Earth.

evidence.quote: the Physicall body of Man, which is nourished from the Earth, and Sydereall body which liveth by the Firmament
but the Invisible, Insensible, Sydereall body (which is the house or cottage of the Spirits life) is from the Astra's of the Firmament
Thus Adam had two bodies, that is, a visible Elementall, and an invisible Sydereall body
but the invisible Sydereall body that is capable of attaining Phylosophy is from the Astra's of the Firmament
Now whereas Man had his Sydereall body from the Astra's of the Firmament

senses.sense: Something every thing, sensible or insensible, has in it, named beside the sydereall spirit (margin note only).

evidence.quote: That which is sensible and that which is insensible hath a sydereall spirit or a sydereall body in it

senses.sense: The first principle, from which one of two kinds of death comes (margin note only).

evidence.quote: There is a two fold death, from the Iliad or first principle, and from the Ens or Being

senses.sense: That whose resolution brings a death the physician's industry can hinder, as against death from the Ens or Being, which cannot be.

evidence.quote: Paracelsus saith that the death which is from the resolution of the Iliad may be hindred by the industry of the Physitian, but that which is from the Ens or Being cannot

senses.sense: Something that contains all things in itself, named where diseases come from the minerals of man. Reading 1: man himself. Basis: the paragraph says there are as many minerals in man as in the world, and MICRO.17 says man carries the world in himself. Reading 2: the first principle, as N307 glosses the word. Basis: N307. (Margin note only; rests on one word of the translation.)

evidence.quote: Many diseases proceed out of the mineralls of man, which Iliad containeth all things in it selfe

senses.sense: Of diseases: springing from the Firmament, in man or from the impressions of the stars, as against elementary diseases; they have astral remedies.

evidence.quote: There are other diseases whereof the most part are Astrall or Firmamentall
which spring out of the Firmament of Man
those acute and pernicious Astrall diseases, the Pleuresie, Plague.
which diseases proceeding from the impressions of the Stars the universall medicine powerfull expelleth
but also those Chronicall, Astrall and fixed diseases which by many are accounted desperate
Elementary diseases are cured by Elemental means, and Astrall have Astrall remedies

senses.sense: Of man's invisible part from the stars: the Astrall body, spirit or man, which is the subject of human reason, sense and wisdom.

evidence.quote: that Astrall body or Syderiall Spirit, which is the true Astrall Man
which Astrall Spirit is the subject of humane Reason that containeth the sences and wisdome in it
The invisible Body or true Internall Man consisting of Reason and an Astrall Spirit, agreeth with the Angells
nor know any thing of the Creation and composition of the internall Astrall Man

senses.sense: Of the chief medicine's nature, by which it recovered a dying man.

evidence.quote: was recovered by its Fiery, Astrall, and Celestiall Invisible Nature

senses.sense: Of a kind of physician, to whom knowing the philosophical secret is principally necessary.

evidence.quote: To know this Phylosophicall Secret truly is principally necessary to an Astrall Physitian

senses.sense: Mastership: Nature's own, in which it makes itself merry (margin note only).

evidence.quote: Nature many times makes it selfe merry with its magistery or mastership and rejoyceth in its master, and in its art and vertues

senses.sense: The philosophers' work itself, into which Lully searched and whose origin a margin note heads; here tied to the matter of the Elixer.

evidence.quote: Raymund Lully that fearcher into this Magistery
the matter of the Elixer
The originall of the Philosophicall Magistery

senses.sense: The work of this Art, what is hidden in which God opens to the Artist.

evidence.quote: that he may open to him what is hid in the magistery of this Art

senses.sense: A kind of prepared medicine, counted among the Arcana beside Fift Essences and named with Elixirs.

evidence.quote: Of this sort are the Fift Essences, Magisteryes, and the like
to learn the preparations of those high Magisteryes and Elixirs

senses.sense: The matter of things as they now stand, set against the first matter in which they were created perfect: the Chymist perfects it by fire and draws the secret things out of it.

evidence.quote: ALL things in respect of the first matter were created perfect, but the Chymist perfecteth the last matter by Fire
by the secret things or Astra's which the Chymist can reduce out of the last matter into the first

senses.sense: In digestion: the last matter of food, out of which the first Ens of the body's nourishment arises by the Archaeus.

evidence.quote: The first Ens or Being toward life, from whence the body hath it's nourishment & food ariseth out of the last matter of the Meat by the Archaeus

senses.sense: Hidden things drawn by the Chymist out of the last matter, neither cold nor hot, which remove diseases; Fift Essences and Magisteryes are of this sort.

evidence.quote: These Arcana or hid things are actually neither cold nor hot yet removeth all diseases
Of this sort are the Fift Essences, Magisteryes, and the like

senses.sense: The secret things of Nature that the better sort of philosophers search out.

evidence.quote: others far more excellent and more truly deserving the name of Philosophers investigate the Arcana and more secret things of Nature
